gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the two '12 hours' figures it put side by side measure different things: Jabra's 12 h for the Speak2 55 is battery life with no test conditions, while Bose's 12 h for the SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen) is music playback (Bluetooth A2DP at 50% volume) and Bose gives no call-time figure. None of them points out either that 'built-in microphone' covers a 4-mic beamforming speakerphone with a stated 2.3 m pickup, a speakerphone mic Bose gives no count for, and popular speakers such as the JBL Clip 5 that have no mic at all.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Jabra Speak2 55 overview (jabra.com) and the cited Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen product page (bose.com). Each one gives its own part on its own: Jabra lists 4 mics, 2.3 m pickup and up to 12 h battery, and Bose footnotes 12 h at A2DP 50% volume. Neither puts the two figures on the same basis, and neither says the Bose has no published call time. No result, cited or not, mentions speakers that have no microphone (JBL Clip 5). The Bose support spec page (result 6) returned no content, and I couldn't open JBL's own pages (HTTP 403).
decides: This backs the split ChatGPT made but tightens it. For calls, only the Jabra gives a pickup range (2.3 m, room up to 4.5 × 4.5 m) and four beamforming mics. The Bose is a music speaker that can take calls, and its 12 h is a music figure. Shoppers should check that a 'Bluetooth speaker' has a mic at all: the JBL Clip 5 (which Dealectric lists) does not, and SoundGuys says it cannot take phone calls. The Marshall Emberton III ($179.99, built-in mic, 32+ h) is a music-first alternative to the Bose, but Marshall gives no playtime test conditions, so its 32 h cannot be compared directly with Bose's 12 h.
